title: Wardrobe and Silence
premise: Theo Nystrom has spent thirty years tuning pianos in strangers' houses, reading grief in the pitch of old strings and perfecting a smile that ends conversations. When the auction notice for her childhood home appears — the house where her brother Elias died and where her mother's silence was built into the walls — Theo returns, telling herself she's only there to appraise the piano. But the house's new buyers, a young family, keep asking questions she can't deflect, and her estranged sister Marta arrives to contest the sale. To survive the week, Theo must finally speak the truth about Elias out loud, before the last bus to the old neighborhood is rerouted forever — and she does, in the empty house on the eve of the auction, with Marta listening at the door, choosing memory over the safe silence that kept her alive but never let her live.
about_author: Rosalind Quintana is a former architectural conservator who spent a decade documenting buildings slated for demolition, interviewing the families who once lived in them. She writes in a converted schoolhouse in upstate New York, where she keeps a piano she refuses to have tuned.

chapters.title: The Pitch of Empty Rooms
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. In a client's brownstone, Theo tunes a piano while the owner talks too much; Theo deploys her practiced smile and leaves early. At home, an auction flyer for 14 Alder Street arrives — her childhood house. Emotional beat: the past intruding on a carefully managed present; she almost throws the flyer away, then can't.

chapters.title: Fourteen Alder Street
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. She takes the bus to the old neighborhood 'just to look,' telling herself the rerouted line is coincidence. The house is staged for viewing; a young couple, the Okafors, are measuring rooms and ask if she grew up around here. She lies, then hears the radiators and can't leave. Emotional beat: the body remembering what the smile conceals.

chapters.title: What the Radiators Said
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, with a flashback to childhood. Wandering the empty house, Theo hears in the pipes the sounds of that winter — Elias's boots, her mother's kettle, the argument through the floor. Flashback reveals Elias drowned in the quarry and their mother never spoke of it again. Emotional beat: grief surfacing as physical memory.

chapters.title: The Piano in the Parlor
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The Okafors discover an upright piano left behind and ask Theo, whose card is on the estate agent's list, to assess it. Inside the bench she finds Elias's sheet music and a photograph she's never seen. She agrees to tune it — her first lie of commission. Emotional beat: complicity with her own avoidance, and the first crack in it.

chapters.title: Marta at the Door
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Marta arrives from out of state to contest the sale, furious that Theo never told her about the auction. Their argument in the driveway exposes the old fault line: Marta grieved loudly, Theo went silent, and each believes the other betrayed Elias. Emotional beat: sisterhood as wound; the auction becomes a proxy war.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The estate agent values the house; Theo, asked to value the piano, lowballs it hoping to buy it herself and keep Elias's music. She visits her mother's grave for the first time in years and says nothing there either, furious at her own muteness. Emotional beat: the price of silence compounding with interest.

chapters.title: Buyer's Remorse
chapters.summary: Adaeze Okafor's POV. Adaeze, restoring the house, finds Elias's initials carved under a windowsill and asks Theo who he was. Theo's deflection fails for the first time — her smile doesn't work — and she walks out mid-sentence. Adaeze recognizes a family's unfinished grief; she and her husband debate delaying the closing. Emotional beat: a stranger's compassion forcing the door open.

chapters.title: The Rerouting
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The city announces the bus line's permanent reroute, and Marta reveals she's found their mother's unopened letters about Elias — she never read them, mirroring Theo's silence. The sisters fight, then sit in the parked car outside the house as the last old-route bus passes. Emotional beat: despair transmuting into resolve; the deadline becomes real.

chapters.title: Out Loud
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, climax. On the eve of the auction, Theo enters the empty house at dusk, sits at the untuned piano, and speaks Elias's name and the whole truth — that she was supposed to walk him to the quarry, that their mother's silence taught her hers. Marta, who followed her, hears everything from the hallway and comes in. Emotional beat: confession as release; the house finally allowed to be a home again.

chapters.title: Tuning
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, coda. At the auction, Theo and Marta bid together and lose the house — but the Okafors invite them back to hear the tuned piano and see Elias's initials preserved under glass. On the rerouted bus, Theo talks the whole way home, and Marta listens. Emotional beat: survival redefined — not the silence that got her through, but the voice she finally has.
